headline: Highest risk is medium: ctx can read/write filesystem and use MCP/browser tooling, while pathway is local-only and non-networked, so the pair mainly creates prompt-injection and data-handling exposure rather than direct exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code post-tool events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem access, so it may ingest content that pathway produces if they share a workspace or handoff. pathway itself has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file I/O surfaces, so the bridge is indirect and uncertainty is higher; I choose medium over low because shared-file ingestion is plausible in default developer setups.
conditions: IF ctx reads files or MCP messages originating from pathway outputs, then attacker-controlled text can influence ctx instructions.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or log file, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of pathway outputs by ctx.
Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Add provenance tags to any handoff files.
Require manual review before ctx acts on pathway-generated text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and filesystem data classes, but pathway has no read_filesystem, write_filesystem, or network egress, so there is no clear path for pathway to leak ctx data onward. The main risk is local workspace exposure if both are pointed at the same files; that is smaller than medium because pathway cannot transmit data off-host.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same filesystem tree, pathway can observe files ctx writes there.
IF ctx stores sensitive logs in a shared directory, local disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict ctx log retention to non-sensitive data.
Mount shared folders read-only where possible.
Review file permissions before running both agents.
requires-engineering: add per-agent encryption at rest.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and install packages, while pathway explicitly cannot write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or execute_shell. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only overlap is ctx’s side of the pair. Because pathway lacks mutable capabilities, the conflict pathway is limited and low severity.
conditions: IF ctx and pathway are pointed at the same writable directory, ctx may overwrite files pathway expects to remain stable.
IF an external orchestrator gives pathway hidden write access, the conflict assessment changes upward.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git checkout.
Serialize any file-producing steps.
Check for stale outputs before ctx writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can generate tool-driven outputs from browser and MCP activity, and pathway is a document-processing agent that could consume those outputs as inputs. There is no evidence pathway verifies upstream claims, so a bad ctx output could cascade into downstream processing. I choose medium because the pairwise handoff is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF pathway ingests ctx-produced files without validation, then ctx errors can propagate downstream.
IF ctx outputs are treated as authoritative source material, cascading factual errors become likely.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require checksum or schema validation on ctx outputs.
Keep pathway inputs read-only until verified.
Log source provenance for every handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and no regulated data class is explicitly listed for pathway, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data. The only concrete compliance concern is retention or residency mismatch if those logs contain sensitive material and are shared with pathway; that is a limited, local policy issue rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF ctx logs contain regulated data and are copied into pathway-managed storage, retention policy mismatch can occur.
IF pathway is deployed in a different residency boundary than ctx, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Classify ctx logs before sharing.
Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Set explicit retention limits for both agents.
Document residency for any shared storage.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
